data.name: grant
data.source: DescribeGrantQuery — the one source of the consent wording; tests/connection/consent.test.ts fails if it softens

data.name: declined
data.source: searchParams — the OAuth error value the callback returned when the user declined at BattleGrid

data.name: failure
data.source: searchParams — the callback's own refusal of a response it could not use

components.purpose: Say exactly what is being granted, before anyone is sent anywhere.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-6, p-6 — the standard shell. On a personal deployment the whole page is the nothing-to-connect component instead; no consent and no button are offered because there is nothing to grant. Both ?declined= and ?error= render when both are present — the notice above the danger banner, in that order — so the two are not exclusive states.
constraints: The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS.

On a personal deployment neither the consent summary nor the start button may render — the button would build an /authorize URL with an empty client_id (requirement: A Remedy Named Must Exist In That Deployment).

components.purpose: Acknowledge the decline the user chose at BattleGrid, in the platform's own value, with the retry visible below.
components.current_implementation: Notice role (rounded-gc-2 border-notice-border bg-notice-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary), role=status — the user chose; nothing failed. Landed by returned-with-an-explanation.
constraints: role=status must survive — a decline is advisory, never announced as an error.
Wears notice, never danger — 'a user who learns to fear advisories learns to abandon valid work' (system.json principle).
The platform's error value renders verbatim.
Every message states nothing was stored — spec scenario 'The user declines' promises the explanation with the retry.

components.purpose: Say why a returned authorization could not be used — incomplete, untrusted, or a value named verbatim.
components.current_implementation: Danger role (rounded-gc-2 border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary), role=alert, opening with a semibold 'No connection was made:' prefix. Landed by returned-with-an-explanation.
constraints: role=alert must survive.
Unknown error values render verbatim, never invented into a friendlier sentence.
States that nothing was stored and that starting again is safe.

components.purpose: What Grid-Commander will be able to do, in words that are true — including that this is not view-only access.
components.current_implementation: aria-labelledby section: h2, plain bullet list of permissions, then DT-0005's hierarchy — the honesty sentence in the consequence role (rounded-gc-2 border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary) and the Not requested block in quiet. Wording verbatim from DescribeGrantQuery, guarded by tests/connection/consent.test.ts.
constraints: The wording comes from DescribeGrantQuery and must render verbatim — requirement 'Configuration Authority Is Described Honestly' forbids calling this read-only, and tests/connection/consent.test.ts fails if it softens.
The honesty sentence ('This is not view-only access…') must not be demoted below the permissions it qualifies, hidden behind interaction, or reduced to fine print.
'Grid-Commander cannot move your funds' stays with the not-requested list.
aria-labelledby wiring on the section must survive.

components.purpose: The authority deliberately not asked for — wager scope — so the absence is stated, not implied.
components.current_implementation: DT-0005: quiet role — rounded-gc-2 border-quiet-border bg-quiet-subtle p-4 — h3 'Not requested', the withheld permissions, and the cannot-move-your-funds sentence verbatim. Visibly lighter than the consequence block above it.
constraints: Rendered only when the grant names withheld permissions — an empty box would claim an absence the query did not state.
The cannot-move-your-funds sentence renders verbatim.

components.purpose: Send the user to BattleGrid to authorize — the page's one action, and the retry after a decline.

actions.effect: Server action: builds the authorization URL and redirects to BattleGrid

components.current_implementation: A form with a single BUTTON_PRIMARY submit, 'Continue to BattleGrid'. No pending state between click and redirect (the product-wide gap, #153).
constraints: Exactly one way in — no second control may start an authorization.
Styling goes through BUTTON_PRIMARY in control.ts.
Sits below the consent summary — nobody is offered the button before the words it agrees to.

components.purpose: On a personal deployment: there is no authorization to grant, and the remedy for a broken key is named from the one source.
components.current_implementation: Own full-page shell: h1 'There is nothing to connect', two explanatory paragraphs (the remedy sentence from describeRemedy — same source as the failure message), and an underlined sentence link back to the agents.
constraints: The remedy sentence comes from describeRemedy('repair-the-key') and must not be paraphrased — two copies would become two answers.
No consent summary and no start button may render here.

flows.name: Connect an account
steps: read what will be granted and what is not requested

flows.name: Decline and come back
steps: return to /connect with the decline acknowledged in notice
the consent summary and button below are the retry

flows.name: A response the product refuses
steps: callback rejects an incomplete or untrusted response
return to /connect with the failure stated in danger
nothing stored; starting again is safe

accessibility.notes: Decline carries role=status, failures role=alert. The consent section is aria-labelledby its heading. No client JS; every state is a full navigation.
